set_aside.subject: store_spool.spool_entry_name
set_aside.question: What exact inputs, output, validation failures and callers define spool_entry_name?
options: Take a SpooledFileKey and return one bounded relative entry name without I/O
Take the key fields separately and return a path component
Keep this as a private helper rather than a public capability
set_aside.default_guess: Take a SpooledFileKey and return one bounded relative entry name without I/O or errors.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool.spool_attempt_prefix
set_aside.question: What exact attempt identity does spool_attempt_prefix accept, what does it return, and what guarantee makes it select all and only files of that attempt?
options: Accept run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number and return a bounded relative prefix
Accept a dedicated attempt-key model and return an opaque selector
Keep attempt selection private to discard_spool_attempt
set_aside.default_guess: Accept the producing attempt fields and return a bounded relative prefix that is disjoint from every other attempt's prefix.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool.publish_spool_entry
set_aside.question: What are publish_spool_entry's exact inputs, output, error categories, filesystem effects and caller obligations, including whether expected digest and size are supplied or computed?
options: Take spool root, SpooledFileKey, bytes, expected digest and size; return publication facts
Take spool root, key and bytes; compute and return digest and size
Take an initialized spool handle, key and a byte stream
set_aside.default_guess: Take an initialized spool area, SpooledFileKey and bytes, compute and verify digest and size, and return digest and size with distinct ceiling-refusal and internal-I/O outcomes.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool.read_spool_entry
set_aside.question: What exact key and expected facts does read_spool_entry receive, what bytes or metadata does it return, and how are a missing entry, symlink, I/O failure, size mismatch and digest mismatch reported to store?
options: Take a SpooledFileKey plus expected digest and size and return bytes
Take a complete SpooledFile and return bytes
Take only a key and derive verification facts elsewhere
set_aside.default_guess: Take a complete SpooledFile identity with expected digest and size, return its bytes, and report every missing, link, I/O or integrity failure as an internal storage error.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool.discard_spool_attempt
set_aside.question: What inputs, idempotence rule and failure result define discarding an attempt, especially when only some files can be removed?
options: Idempotently remove all files selected by an attempt key and report any incomplete removal as internal error
Require every expected entry key and remove that explicit set
Make discard part of publish_spool_entry's ceiling-refusal result with no separately callable operation
set_aside.default_guess: Idempotently remove every entry under the attempt's exact prefix and return internal error if complete removal cannot be confirmed.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_group
set_aside.question: What identifies a spool group, is removing an absent group successful, and how are link and I/O failures returned to store?
options: A group is run_id; removal is idempotent and failures are reported
A group is an opaque run-directory key created by store_spool
Absence and all removal failures are silently accepted
set_aside.default_guess: Use run_id as the group key, treat absence as success, and report link or I/O failures for store.remove_run_spool to suppress where required.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_temporaries
set_aside.question: What directory scope is scanned, which names count as temporaries, whether the scan also performs the required start-time symlink check, and which failures stop startup are not fixed.
options: Scan the entire spool area, reject any symlink, remove only emitted temporary names, and report failures
Remove known temporary names only while store performs a separate symlink scan
Best-effort removal that never stops startup
set_aside.default_guess: Scan the whole spool area at startup, refuse any symlink, remove only the module's temporary-name pattern, and propagate scan or removal failures so startup stops.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: store_spool initialization and spool-root ownership
set_aside.text: The spool's on-disk layout below the spool area and the run directory, the temporary names, the ceiling accounting and the attempt discard.
set_aside.question: How does store_spool receive and retain the spool-area root while exposing no initialization or construction capability and accepting no documented root argument?
options: store constructs a store_spool object with the spool root during open_store
Every store_spool operation receives the spool root explicitly
store_spool derives a process-global root from configuration
set_aside.default_guess: store constructs an instance bound to the spool root during open_store and keeps that handle privately.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: spool_run_bytes_max accounting during replacement
set_aside.text: the run's spooled files plus this one against spool_run_bytes_max
set_aside.question: When publishing replaces an unnamed file already at the same position, is the run ceiling checked against current total plus the full new size, or current total minus the replaced entry's size plus the new size; and do temporary files count?
options: Subtract the replaced entry and add the new entry; temporaries do not count
Add the new size to the current total before replacement; temporaries do not count
Count all regular files below the run directory, including temporaries
set_aside.default_guess: Use the resulting published-entry total: subtract the replaced entry's size, add the new size, and exclude temporary files.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state

set_aside.subject: startup symlink validation of the spool area
set_aside.text: refusing a symbolic link anywhere below the spool area
set_aside.question: Which store_spool operation performs the exhaustive startup check required by A18 for links already present anywhere in the spool, since the listed capabilities contain no explicit validation operation?
options: remove_spool_temporaries also scans every entry and refuses any symlink
open_store performs the scan without using store_spool
Add a separate store_spool validation/open operation
set_aside.default_guess: Treat remove_spool_temporaries as a full no-follow traversal that first refuses any symlink and then removes emitted temporaries.
set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
